method: Rebuilt the 240-item unreferenced pack after a fresh factual and ambiguity review. Read publisher vocabulary/phrase tables, government-sponsored Peace Corps lessons, Abu Dhabi Culture definitions, Al Ramsa Institute sample textbook, and NYU CAMeL Maknuune v1.0.1 lexical entries. Scanned 1992 Darija appendix pages were downloaded from US Department of Education ERIC and visually read because OCR damaged Arabic. Question text is newly edited, not an automatic first-eight selection.
difficulty: Editorial targets .80/.60/.40/.25/.15 for mixed Arabic-speaking families 16+; not measured. Basic media-familiar terms first, local household and kinship terms in middle tiers, narrow material-culture terms in hardest tiers. Native speakers of the represented regions will find local words easier.

editorialDecisions: Semantic topics provide ten substantive areas. Geographic labels specify Egyptian, Emirati, Moroccan or Palestinian usage; they do not claim exclusivity or collapse all Gulf dialects into one.

Polysemous words receive context: عيان means tired in the quoted Moroccan bedtime/comfort setting; شختورة is restricted to the boat sense; معاش to employment; وايد to adjective intensification; طشة to an outing.

Removed etymology guesses, uncited culinary trivia, duplicate translations and inherited verified flags without proof. Old IDs are replaced by 901–908; global retired-ID registration is handled by the bank rebuild owner.
Did not accept الزبيل for الديين: official pearl-diving source calls the former a rope and the latter a collection basket.
No fabricated sources, no empirical pass-rate claim, and no change to game logic, bank status, or other editors files.
